newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parties seek election delay after flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish parties seek election delay after flood.

text.p: Most Polish political parties demanded on Wednesday that a September 21 general election be delayed because of heavy floods, but the ruling ex-communists insisted on keeping to the date.

The parties -- from the opposition Union for Freedom (UW) to the Peasant Party, junior partner in the government coalition -- said the president should declare a state of emergency in flood-hit areas which would automatically postpone the polls.
"This is no time, no atmosphere for elections. Reconstructing flooded areas is the priority now," UW spokesman Andrzej Potocki told Reuters.
He suggested that the polls could be staged in November.
By law, the election can be held no sooner than three months after the end of a state of emergency.

Advocates say a state of emergency would facilitate the repair of damage caused by the floods, the worst in centuries, which put more than 5,000 sq km (2,000 sq miles) of Poland's south and west under water and killed 55 people.
But President Aleksander Kwasniewski, linked to the principal governing party, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), refused to introduce the measure.
He said in Szczecin that there would be enough time to help flooded communities recover sufficiently to hold the polls as planned, PAP news agency reported.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, an ex-communist, said the polls should take place as scheduled because "it would be a sign that Poland is a stable country, which even in the face of serious trouble...respects democratic rules".

But some officials of the Peasant Party said the current parliament and government should stay in place until flood damage was repaired and next year's budget had been passed by the existing parliament.

"A change of government would disrupt the relief and reconstruction process. I think that in the circumstances the current coalition should take full resposibility for the 1998 budget," senior Peasant Party official Janusz Piechocinski said.
"I think the optimal election date is early spring."
Cimoszewicz wants to offer his government's budget draft to the next parliament after the election, when the line-up may be different from now.
The Peasant Party leadership will meet on Friday to decide whether to support the planned parliamentary motion, already backed by the opposition, demanding a state of emergency.

The party will also review the option of quickly amending the current constitution to allow a postponement of the polls, but such an amendment would be very unlikely to pass in parliament as the ex-communists have enough votes to block it.

The biggest opposition group, the Solidarity Election Alliance (AWS), whose current popularity is greater than its representation in parliament, said it would also back a state of emergency delaying the polls.
"The election date is of no importance. What matters is the help for flood victims," said spokesman Tomasz Tywonek of the AWS, the strongest challenger to the ruling party.
Tywonek charged that the ex-communists did not want to move the date because this would hit their showing at the ballot.

He said the ex-communists thought widespread discontent over government handling of the flood crisis would not be visible if the polls were held as scheduled, because the exhausted flood victims might not vote in large numbers. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
